body: THE GOOD NUMBER: India's third-largest housing financier grew AUM ~33% to ~Rs 1.1 lakh cr in FY18 (Motilal Oswal), loan book Rs 91,932 cr (+28%), profit growth ~25%, low reported NPAs, valuation below HDFC. WHY IT LIED: the growth mix shifted to project/developer and other non-retail loans (project loans +55% YoY in Q3 FY18, non-retail +52% YoY), and much of it went to little-known entities later alleged to be linked to the Wadhawan promoters (Cobrapost: ~Rs 31,000 cr). The book was long-dated but funded with commercial paper and MF money. Low NPAs in a fast-growing book are mechanical: new loans have not had time to default. When IL&FS defaulted (Sep 2018) and DSP MF dumped DHFL paper, refinancing froze; default June 2019; equity wiped out in the 2021 Piramal resolution. TEST: for lenders read growth by segment, ALM buckets (1-year gap), CP share of liabilities, top-20 borrower exposure and related-party links; compare NPAs against loans seasoned 2-3 years (lagged NPA), not today's book. LESSON: in a lender, fast growth plus low NPAs is the ingredients list of a future problem unless funding is long and the book is granular retail.

data.good_number: AUM ~Rs 1.1 lakh cr, +33% YoY in FY18; profits +25%; low gross NPAs; cheap vs HDFC
data.test_that_catches_it: ALM gap in 1-year bucket; share of CP funding; wholesale/project loan growth vs retail; borrower concentration and promoter links
data.why_misleading: growth came from developer/project and wholesale loans (project loans +55% YoY), many to promoter-linked entities, funded by short-term CP/MF money

title: Hidden trap: DHFL's 33% AUM growth and low reported NPAs
